players.product: utility T&D grid infrastructure (transmission/substation connectors and hardware up to 765 kV, System Control control houses) and data-center electrical components (Burndy connectors, PCX power skids, 800 V pin & sleeve devices)

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center demand vs capacity (VP IR Dan Innamorato): in the short-cycle part of the business, where Hubbell books and ships components in 4 to 6 weeks, 'it's just hard to commit to 50% growth at the beginning of the year with nothing in backlog'; through the year, 'particularly again on the Burndy side, is every time we added more capacity and were able to ship more product, the orders kept going up', and Hubbell is 'planning our capacity for more growth than that'. CEO Gerben Bakker: in hindsight the beginning-of-year projection was 'probably a little bit conservative'; outperformance came from the capacity it added and new balance-of-system products; he believes 'there is durability to data center', with the pace depending on whether utilities can support the load.
quarterly_data.figure: short-cycle components shipped in 4 to 6 weeks; capacity planned for more than 50% data-center growth

quarterly_data.signal: Beyond data centers (VP IR Dan Innamorato): through 2026 growth has broadened - light industrial has picked up and the long-soft non-residential side has picked up, with activity regionally mapping 'very closely to where data centers are going in'; heavy industrial is still a little softer. CEO Gerben Bakker: utility customers are giving visibility further out and utility capital budgets now reflect longer-duration substation and transmission projects; Hubbell products are still relatively short lead time (weeks to a couple of months), but lead times are 'extending in some of the product lines where we're more constrained', and Hubbell is investing to bring them back down. On 765 kV it has 'one award already that we'll start shipping next year'.
quarterly_data.figure: lead times of weeks to a couple of months, extending in constrained product lines

quarterly_data.signal: Grid automation / Aclara (CEO Gerben Bakker): Hubbell has reassessed its AMI strategy - its investment ramp to break into investor-owned utilities 'proved just more difficult', so it is now focused on public power (co-ops and municipal utilities), where it is traditionally strong, and has taken cost out. Utilities are delaying next-generation AMI upgrades while investing elsewhere, but more aging meters are failing, driving MRO replacement; after several quarters of decline he expects Aclara to turn to modest growth by the end of the year, with a view 'much more modest' than the rest of the portfolio; controls and protection devices are 'going really nicely'.

800 VDC and targets (CEO Gerben Bakker): Burndy grounding products will change little, while Pin and Sleeve devices are being developed for higher amperages now and 'eventually the 800 VDC infrastructure'; for power skids the equipment on them 'will probably go through a lot of change' and Hubbell is working with customers and the gear manufacturers to prepare. Hubbell has exceeded the long-term targets it set in 2024 (restructuring, electrical segment unification 'still in the middle innings', DMC and NSI acquisitions), and ahead of the 2027 investor day 'our view is incrementally positive on what the targets are going to be going forward' because underlying demand is stronger than anticipated. Metals inflation is being priced and prices are sticking.
